overview.summary: Biotechnology brings about artificial genetic changes and uses cells and their products. It gives insulin, interferon, interleukin, vaccines, gene therapy and stem cell research for health; BT cotton, biofertilizers and biopesticides for agriculture; artificial insemination and embryo transfer for animal husbandry; and DNA fingerprinting for forensic science. Organ donation after death saves lives. Green, white and blue revolutions increased food, milk and aquatic production.
youWillLearn: Define biotechnology, cloning and stem cells
Name biotechnology products used against diseases
Explain GM crops, biofertilizers and biopesticides
Describe DNA fingerprinting and its use
Understand organ donation and food preservation

entries.question: • Nowadays, safer vaccines are being produced.
entries.answer:
(1) Before the advent of biotechnology, the vaccines were made from inactive or dead pathogens of that disease.

(2) But now the vaccine is made artificially using biotechnological processes.

(3) Such vaccines produced some disease symptoms in some cases.

(4) The antigen of the disease is researched upon and its genetic code is found out.

(5) A similar antigen is made in the laboratories which is used as a vaccine.

(6) Such vaccines are more thermostable and remain active for longer duration. Therefore, the vaccines are now safer.

notes.title: Q. Set 8 : Rules, Theories, Laws, Definitions and Principles

entries.question: Stem cell
entries.answer: The special cells having pluripotency and ability to divide and differentiate into new cells are called stem cells.

entries.question: Biotechnology
entries.answer: Technology that brings about artificial genetic changes and hybridization in organisms for human welfare is called biotechnology.

entries.question: Genetically modified crops
entries.answer: Crops having desired characters are developed by integrating foreign gene with their genome, such crops have modified genome and are known as genetically modified crops.

entries.question: Vaccine
entries.answer: The ‘antigen’ containing material given to a person or animal to acquire either permanent or temporary immunity against a specific pathogen or disease is called a vaccine.

entries.question: Cloning
entries.answer: Production of replica of any cell or organ or entire organism through biotechnological process is called cloning.

entries.question: Green revolution
entries.answer: All the methods applied for harvesting maximum yield from minimum land are collectively referred to as green revolution.

entries.question: • DNA fingerprinting. (March ’24) (2 marks)
entries.answer:
(1) As the fingerprints are unique for every individual, similarly the nucleotide sequence in the DNA molecule is also unique.

(2) By knowing this sequence, one can find out the identity of any person. Such technique to establish the identity of a person by taking into consideration the nucleotide sequence is called DNA fingerprinting.

(3) Its main use is in forensic sciences to confirm the identity of the criminal.

(4) Similarly, identity of parents in case of disputed parentage for any child can be understood by taking DNA fingerprints of both the parents and a child.

Stem cells are present in the by which the foetus is joined to the uterus of the mother. Stem cells are also present in the stage of embryonic development. Stem cells are present in and of adult human beings. It has become possible to produce different types of tissues and the part of any organ with the help of these stem cells.
entries.answer: Differentiation of stem cells can form various tissues in the body. Stem cells are present in the umbilical cord by which the foetus is joined to the uterus of the mother. Stem cells are also present in the blastocyst stage of embryonic development. Stem cells are present in red bone marrow and adipose connective tissue of adult human beings. It has become possible to produce different types of tissues and the degenerated part of any organ with the help of these stem cells.

entries.question: (1) What is the liberal view behind the organ and body donation?
entries.answer: By body donation, research in medical studies is possible. The needy persons can get vital organs which can save their lives.

entries.question: (2) Name any four organs that can be donated.
entries.answer: Liver, kidneys, heart, eyes, skin, etc. can be donated.

entries.question: (1) What are edible vaccines?
entries.answer:
(1) Edible vaccines are those which are given as a food by incorporating them into the foodstuff.

(2) Such edible vaccines are produced through biotechnology.

(3) Transgenic potatoes are produced with the help of biotechnology which contain vaccine that act against bacteria like Vibrio cholerae, Escherichia coli.

(4) If raw potatoes are consumed, then the immunity is generated in the body of a person. However, eating only raw potatoes generates the immunity against cholera and the disease caused due to E. coli.

entries.question: (2) Define genetically modified crops and give any two examples. (March ’22)
entries.answer:
(1) Definition of genetically modified crops : Crops having desired characters are developed by integrating foreign gene with their genome, such crops have modified genome and are known as genetically modified crops.

(2) Examples of genetically modified crops : BT cotton, BT Brinjal and Golden rice are the GMOs.

entries.question: (3) What is DNA Fingerprinting? Where is it mainly useful? (March ’24)
entries.answer:
(1) DNA fingerprint : The nucleotic sequence present on the DNA of each person is unique just like the fingerprint, thus for establishing the identity of any person DNA can be analysed, this technique is known as DNA fingerprinting.

(2) Uses of DNA fingerprinting : (i) Investigations used in forensic sciences. (ii) To establish identity of the criminal. (iii) To identify parents of any child in case of disputed parentage.

entries.question: (1) What is stem cell? Write any four uses of stem cell. (March ’25)
entries.answer:
Stem cells : The special cells having pluripotency and ability to divide and differentiate into new cells are called Stem cells. They are present in multicellular living beings. Uses of stem cells :

(1) Stem cells are used for regenerative therapy.

(2) In case of diseased conditions like diabetes, myocardial infarction, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, etc. Stem cells can be used to replace the damaged or functionless, cells.

(3) In conditions such as anaemia, thalassaemia, leukaemia, etc., there is always the need of newer blood cells. Here, stem cells can be used to restore the number of blood cells.

(4) In techniques of organ transplantation, stem cells can be used and they can help in the transplantation of new organs such as kidney and liver. The defective organs can be replaced by those that defective organs are produced with the help of stem cells and transplanted.

entries.question: (2) Answer the following questions : (a) What is Biotechnology? (b) Give one use of Biotechnology. (c) Give one commercial use of Biotechnology. (d) Write two bacterial examples of biofertilizer. (e) Write two names of crops genetically developed. (March ’20) (5 marks)
entries.answer: (a) Biotechnology : Technology that brings about artificial genetic changes and hybridisation in organisms for human welfare is called biotechnology. (b) Biotechnology is very useful in improving the yield and variety of agricultural products. (c) Commercial use of Biotechnology : Production of hormones, interferons, antibiotics and different vaccines. (d) Rhizobium and Azotobacter are used to prepare natural fertilizers. (e) Genetically modified crops : Golden Rice and Bt. Cotton.

entries.question: (3) Explain the following terms : (a) Stem cells (b) Cloning (c) Genetically modified crops (March ’24) (3 marks)
entries.answer: (a) Stem cells: Special cells with the ability to divide and differentiate into different cell types. (b) Cloning: The production of a genetically identical copy of a cell, organism or other biological material. (c) Genetically modified crops: Crops whose genomes have been altered by introducing desired foreign genes to give them specific characteristics.

entries.question: (4) Which precautions will you take during spraying of pesticides? (Sept. ’21) (3 marks)
entries.answer:
(1) Pesticides are toxic chemicals. By using them indiscriminately, they contaminate the water, soil and also crops.

(2) The D.D.T., chloropyriphos and malathion are very dangerous. They spread through the food chain causing biomagnification.

(3) Therefore, we shall not use such insecticides and pesticides. We shall use organic pesticides.

(4) At the time of spraying, nose, eyes and skin will be covered and protected.

(5) Care will be taken not to allow children or domestic animals to come in contact with a pesticide.

(6) Excessive use will not be done.

entries.question: (5) Answer the following questions : (3 marks) (a) What is meant by green revolution? (b) Who is a father of green revolution in India? (c) What is AMUL and who was the founder director of AMUL ?
entries.answer: (a) Green revolution is collective method used in agriculture practices where different methods are used to harvest maximum yield from minimum land. (b) Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is a father of green revolution in India. (c) AMUL means Anand Milk Union Limited whose founder director was Dr. Verghese Kurien.
